Willard Richards

24 June 1804–11 Mar. 1854. Teacher, lecturer, doctor, clerk, printer, editor, postmaster. Born at Hopkinton, Middlesex Co., Massachusetts. Son of Joseph Richards and Rhoda Howe. Moved to Richmond, Berkshire Co., Massachusetts, 1813; to Chatham, Columbia Co...

View Full Bio
a comfortable house, in common with the rest of his fellow laborers in the vineyard of the Lord,
1

Many of the wives and children of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles lived in poverty while their husbands and fathers preached in England between 1837 and 1841. Some of the men built permanent homes in Nauvoo when they returned from England, including Brigham Young, Parley P. Pratt, and Orson Hyde in 1843 and Wilford Woodruff in 1844. Similar to Richards’s subscription, a collection was taken on 4 July 1843 to help build Hyde’s house. (Hyrum Smith, Nauvoo, IL, to Parley P. Pratt, New York City, NY, 22 Dec. 1839, in JS Letterbook 2, p. 81; Vilate Murray Kimball, Nauvoo, IL, to Heber C. Kimball, 6 Sept. or Oct. 1840, typescript, Heber C. Kimball Family Organization, Compilation of Heber C. Kimball Correspondence, 1983, CHL; Phebe Carter Woodruff, Lee Co., Iowa Territory, to Wilford Woodruff, Manchester, England, 6–19 Oct. 1840, pp. [3]–[4], digital scan; Phebe Carter Woodruff, Montrose, Iowa Territory, to Wilford Woodruff, London, England, 25 Oct.–2 Nov. 1840, pp. [1], [3], digital scan, Wilford Woodruff, Collection, 1831–1905, CHL; Marinda Nancy Johnson Hyde, Donation, 29 Jan. 1842, in Book of the Law of the Lord, 71; Wells, “Biography of Mary Ann Angell Young,” 56–57; Helen Mar Kimball Whitney, “Scenes in Nauvoo,” Woman’s Exponent, 15 Sept. 1881, 10:58; “History of Brigham Young,” Deseret News [Salt Lake City], 17 Mar. 1858, 9; Parley P. Pratt, Nauvoo, IL, to John Van Cott, Canaan Four Corners, NY, 7 May 1843, CHL; Richards, Journal, 10 June 1843; JS, Journal, 4 July 1843; Woodruff, Journal, 4 May 1844.)
